images.caption: Figure 1:Overview of learning paradigms for LLM agents, comparing parametric and non-parametric approaches along the dimensions of stored knowledge, inference-time usage, and update mechanism.

Figure 2:Overview of Tutorial Agentic Learning (TAL). In Stage I, TAL performs video-grounded agent–model adversarial consolidation, where a video agent harvests hard question–answer pairs from instructional videos that are supported by tutorial evidence yet unsolved by the frozen model, forming a question bank. In Stage II, TAL performs question–memory adversarial consolidation, using this question bank to iteratively refine tutorial memory through a read–write loop. At inference time, TAL retrieves relevant tutorial units via a Table-of-Contents (TOC) tree, enabling the frozen model to access structured tutorial knowledge for downstream reasoning without parameter updates.
Figure 3:Scaling behavior of TAL vs. vanilla (GPT-5.2) on training (left) and test (right) splits.
Figure 4:Interactive user interface used for human evaluation.
Figure 5:Comparison of learning curves on the held-out test set.
